newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada union hopeful of Ford Canada deal.
newsitem.headline: Canada union hopeful of Ford Canada deal.

text.p: The Canadian Auto Workers union said on Monday it was optimistic a tentative deal with Ford Motor Co of Canada Ltd could be reached as early as tonight after Ford said it would present its economic offer later today.

CAW president Buzz Hargrove said the union could reach a conditional agreement Monday night if the economic package mirrored the pattern deal forged previously with the Canadian units of Chrysler Corp and General Motors Corp.

"If we can resolve all of the issues to our satisfaction and the only thing is language that we will have to work out, we will announce a tentative agreement subject to the language reflecting the agreement in principle we have," said Hargrove.
"There will be an offer made sometime this evening," said Ford spokesman Jim Hartford, who later suggested the offer would come at about 1900 EST/2400 GMT.
Hartford declined to say whether the package would mirror the pattern agreement.
"I think we'll have to wait until (Ford's chief negotiator Donald) McKenzie gets here this evening to find that out," said Hartford.

The framework deal with Chrysler and GM gave the union protection from outsourcing, or contracting out jobs, ensured minimum health and safety and employment standards and gave workers improved benefits and a 10.2 percent wage and cost of living increase over three years.
Both sides said they would meet through the day in an effort to settle lingering local issues, including working conditions at Ford's Oakville, Ontario truck and van assembly plant.
The CAW, which represents about 11,700 Ford workers, has set a strike deadline of 1900 EST/2400 GMT on Wednesday if a deal cannot be reached.
While not ruling out an early settlement, a source close to the union said talks would likely go down to the wire simply because labor pacts were rarely settled two days before a strike deadline.
"I haven't seen many examples of it going early," said the source.
But Hargrove said the early presentation of Ford's economic package left him optimistic a deal could be reached without a work stoppage.

"I'm assuming and hopeful and expecting that (McKenzie) will meet the pattern without much of a fight here," said Hargrove. "When he called us in the middle of our caucus to say that he's going to table a comprehensive economic proposal at seven (o'clock) tonight, that's reason for optimism."

In October, talks between the union and GM Canada broke down after the company presented its economic offer just hours before the strike deadline. The ensuing 20-day strike by 26,000 GM workers disrupted production across North America.
Ford Canada is a wholly owned unit of Ford Motor Co.
